summary: The Storage section states one concrete design fact: transfers go into a month-partitioned transfers table with a covering index on account_id. The rest is boilerplate sentences repeated many times covering logging with request ids, secret rotation, health endpoints, alerting, schema review, a 200 ms p95 read latency target, YAML config, low-priority backfills, unit test coverage, dashboards, and a three-phase migration. No evidence, code, or data supports any of it.

claims.text: Transfers table is partitioned by month with a covering index on account_id.
Read latency target is under 200 ms at the 95th percentile.
The migration ran in three phases over two weekends without downtime.
Alerts route to the payments channel and page after five minutes.
Secrets rotate every ninety days through the platform vault.
Configuration lives in a single YAML file loaded at startup.

risks.note: 200 ms p95 target, five-minute page delay, ninety-day rotation stated with no source.
Migration completed without downtime is asserted with no evidence or date.
Partitioning and index design given without schema or query evidence.
Section is heavily repeated boilerplate; unclear which sentences are real design decisions.

least_confident: I could not tell whether the repeated sentences in L55-L65 are intended content or filler, so I cannot judge which of them a reviewer should treat as real commitments.
